question:
Which soil is the largest available and the most intensively cultivated soil in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Alluvial soil
Desert soil
Red soil
Black soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial soil

Explanation:
Alluvial soil is the most widely available and intensively cultivated soil in India. It is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers and is primarily found in the northern plains and river valleys. This soil is rich in potash, phosphoric acid, and lime, making it highly suitable for crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and others. It is extremely fertile and covers approximately 43% of India's total cultivable land.

Extra Facts:
Alluvial soil is classified into KhadarBhangar (old alluvial). It is spread across the plains of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, Sutlej, and other rivers. The color of this soil ranges from light brown to dark brown. It is not only the most fertile soil in India but also one of the most fertile soils in the world.

भारत में सबसे अधिक उपलब्ध और सबसे अधिक सघन खेती वाली मिट्टी कौन सी है?

options_hi: जलोढ़ मिट्टी
रेगिस्तानी मिट्टी
लाल मिट्टी
काली मिट्टी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है जलोढ़ मिट्टी

Explanation:
भारत में जलोढ़ मिट्टी सबसे अधिक उपलब्ध और सघन खेती वाली मिट्टी है। यह मिट्टी नदियों द्वारा लाए गए अवसादों से बनती है और मुख्य रूप से उत्तरी मैदानों और नदी घाटियों में पाई जाती है। इसमें पोटाश, फॉस्फोरिक एसिड और चूना प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाता है, जो इसे गेहूं, चावल, गन्ना और अन्य फसलों के लिए उपयुक्त बनाता है। यह मिट्टी कृषि के लिए अत्यधिक उपजाऊ है और भारत की कुल कृषि योग्य भूमि का लगभग 43% हिस्सा इसी मिट्टी से ढका हुआ है।

Extra Facts:
जलोढ़ मिट्टी को खादर (नई जलोढ़) और बांगर (पुरानी जलोढ़) में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है। यह मिट्टी गंगा, ब्रह्मपुत्र, सतलज और अन्य नदियों के मैदानों में विस्तृत है। इस मिट्टी का रंग हल्के भूरे से लेकर गहरे भूरे तक होता है। यह मिट्टी न केवल भारत बल्कि विश्व की सबसे उपजाऊ मिट्टियों में से एक है।

question:
Which of the following factors is primarily responsible for soil formation?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Weathering
Irrigation
Degradation
Mining
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Weathering

Explanation:
Weathering is primarily responsible for soil formation. Weathering is a natural process where rocks break down into smaller particles through physical, chemical, and biological processes. Factors like temperature changes, water, wind, vegetation, and organisms contribute to weathering. After weathering, the mixing of organic matter and the passage of time further aid in soil formation. Irrigation, degradation, and mining are not processes of soil formation but factors that affect soil quality.

Extra Facts:
The five main factors of soil formation are: climate, biotic factors, topography, parent material, and time. In India, black soil is formed from the weathering of volcanic rocks and is ideal for cotton cultivation. Red soil is derived from crystalline rock weathering. Soil formation can take hundreds to thousands of years.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कारक मृदा निर्माण के लिए मुख्य रूप से उत्तरदायी है?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: अपक्षय (Weathering)
सिंचाई (Irrigation)
अवक्रमण (Degradation)
खनन (Mining)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अपक्षय (Weathering)

Explanation:
मृदा निर्माण के लिए अपक्षय (Weathering) मुख्य रूप से उत्तरदायी है। अपक्षय एक प्राकृतिक प्रक्रिया है जिसमें चट्टानें भौतिक, रासायनिक और जैविक प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा टूटकर मृदा में परिवर्तित होती हैं। यह प्रक्रिया तापमान परिवर्तन, जल, हवा, वनस्पति और जीवों की गतिविधियों से प्रभावित होती है। मृदा निर्माण में अपक्षय के बाद जैविक पदार्थों का मिश्रण और समय भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। सिंचाई, अवक्रमण और खनन मृदा निर्माण की प्रक्रिया नहीं हैं, बल्कि ये मृदा की गुणवत्ता को प्रभावित करने वाले कारक हैं।

Extra Facts:
मृदा निर्माण के पाँच मुख्य कारक हैं: जलवायु (Climate), जैविक कारक (Biotic factors), उच्चावच (Topography), मूल पदार्थ (Parent material), और समय (Time)। भारत में, काली मृदा (Black soil) ज्वालामुखीय चट्टानों के अपक्षय से बनती है और यह कपास की खेती के लिए उपयुक्त है। लाल मृदा (Red soil) क्रिस्टलीय चट्टानों के अपक्षय से निर्मित होती है। मृदा निर्माण की प्रक्रिया में सैकड़ों से हजारों वर्ष लग सकते हैं।

question:
In a laterite soil profile, which of the following elements is present in an excessive amount?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Iron
feldspar
Nitrogen
Lime
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iron

Explanation:
Laterite soil is found in tropical and subtropical regions where high rainfall and temperature cause intense weathering of the soil. In this process, soluble elements like silica and lime are washed away, while insoluble elements like iron and aluminium accumulate in the soil. Hence, laterite soil contains an excessive amount of iron, giving it a red or yellow color. This soil is less fertile for agriculture due to its low organic matter and nutrient content.

Extra Facts:
Laterite soil is found in parts of Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha, West Bengal, and Assam in India. It is suitable for crops like tea, coffee, cashew, rubber, and coconut, but requires fertilizers to improve fertility. Laterite soil is also used in brick-making as it hardens upon drying. This soil forms due to the leaching process, where soluble minerals are washed away by rainwater.

☛ In which climate is laterite soil found? → Tropical and subtropical
☛ What is deficient in laterite soil? → Nitrogen and organic matter
☛ What is laterite soil used for? → Brick-making
question_hi:
लैटेराइट मृदा परिच्छेदिका (laterite soil profile) में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा तत्व अत्यधिक मात्रा में उपस्थित होता है?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: लोहा (Iron)
पोटाश (feldspar)
नाइट्रोजन (Nitrogen)
चुना (lime)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है लोहा (Iron)

Explanation:
लैटेराइट मृदा उष्णकटिबंधीय और उपोष्णकटिबंधीय क्षेत्रों में पाई जाती है, जहां अधिक वर्षा और उच्च तापमान के कारण मृदा का तीव्र अपक्षय होता है। इस प्रक्रिया में सिलिका (silica) और चूना (lime) जैसे घुलनशील तत्व बह जाते हैं, जबकि लोहा (iron) और एल्युमिनियम (aluminium) जैसे अघुलनशील तत्व मृदा में अधिक मात्रा में जमा हो जाते हैं। इसलिए, लैटेराइट मृदा में लोहा प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाता है, जो इसे लाल या पीले रंग का बनाता है। यह मृदा कृषि के लिए कम उपयोगी होती है क्योंकि इसमें जैविक पदार्थों और पोषक तत्वों की कमी होती है।

Extra Facts:
लैटेराइट मृदा भारत में केरल, कर्नाटक, तमिलनाडु, ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल और असम के कुछ भागों में पाई जाती है। यह मृदा चाय, कॉफी, काजू, रबर और नारियल जैसी फसलों के लिए उपयुक्त है, लेकिन इसमें उर्वरता बढ़ाने के लिए उर्वरकों की आवश्यकता होती है। लैटेराइट मिट्टी का उपयोग ईंट निर्माण में भी किया जाता है क्योंकि यह सूखने पर कठोर हो जाती है। इस मृदा का निर्माण अपक्षालन (leaching) प्रक्रिया के कारण होता है, जिसमें वर्षा जल के साथ घुलनशील पदार्थ बह जाते हैं।

question:
Which type of soil is mostly found in the eastern coast of India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Laterite
Alluvial
Red Rocky
Black Cotton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alluvial

Explanation:
The eastern coast of India is predominantly covered with 'Alluvial soil'. This soil is formed by the deposition of silt, sand, and clay brought by rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, and Mahanadi. These rivers transport sediments from the Himalayas and the Deccan Plateau, making the soil highly fertile. Alluvial soil is ideal for cultivating crops such as rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

Extra Facts:
Apart from alluvial soil, some regions of the eastern coast also have 'Laterite soil', which forms in high-rainfall areas. Alluvial soil is rich in organic matter but lacks nitrogen, phosphorus, and potash. It covers nearly 40% of India's total cultivable land and supports intensive agriculture.

question:
In the realm of soil science, humus is considered:

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: synthetic additive
decaying organic matter in soil
mineral-rich compound
inorganic material
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is decaying organic matter in soil

Explanation:
Humus is a vital component in soil science formed by the decomposition of organic matter in soil. It results from the breakdown of plant and animal residues and plays a crucial role in enhancing soil fertility. Humus provides nutrients, improves water retention, and enhances soil structure. It is the primary constituent of the 'organic fraction' of soil and is often referred to as the 'life of the soil.'

Extra Facts:
Humus is essential for soil as it acts as a reservoir of nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur. It helps maintain soil pH balance and provides a habitat for microorganisms. The presence of humus improves soil drainage and is critical for sustainable agriculture, especially in organic farming.

question_hi:
मृदा विज्ञान के क्षेत्र में ह्यूमस को क्या माना जाता है ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options_hi: सांश्लेषिक योजक
मृदा में क्षयमान कार्बनिक पदार्थ
खनिज समृद्ध यौगिक
अकार्बनिक पदार्थ
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है मृदा में क्षयमान कार्बनिक पदार्थ

Explanation:
ह्यूमस मृदा विज्ञान में मृदा के कार्बनिक पदार्थों के अपघटन से बना एक महत्वपूर्ण घटक है। यह पौधों और जीवों के अवशेषों के विघटन से निर्मित होता है और मृदा की उर्वरता बढ़ाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। ह्यूमस मृदा को पोषक तत्व प्रदान करता है, जल धारण क्षमता बढ़ाता है और मृदा संरचना में सुधार करता है। यह मृदा के 'जैविक भाग' का प्रमुख घटक है और इसे 'मृदा का जीवन' भी कहा जाता है।

Extra Facts:
ह्यूमस मृदा के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह नाइट्रोजन, फॉस्फोरस और सल्फर जैसे पोषक तत्वों का स्रोत है। यह मृदा के pH स्तर को संतुलित रखने में मदद करता है और सूक्ष्मजीवों के लिए आवास प्रदान करता है। ह्यूमस की उपस्थिति से मृदा की जल निकासी क्षमता भी बेहतर होती है। यह कृषि उत्पादकता को बढ़ाने के लिए आवश्यक है और जैविक खेती में इसका विशेष महत्व है।

question:
Which unit is used to measure the concentration of contaminants in soil and sediment ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: DPMO
TDS
PPBB
PPM
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is PPM

Explanation:
PPM (Parts Per Million) is used to measure the concentration of contaminants in soil and sediment. This unit indicates how many parts of a contaminant are present per million parts of the sample. It is a standard unit used in environmental studies, agriculture, and industrial processes. TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) measures dissolved solids in water, while DPMO (Defects Per Million Opportunities) is used in quality control. PPBB is not a valid unit.

Extra Facts:
Soil pollution is a serious environmental issue affecting human health and ecosystems. Heavy metals (e.g., lead, mercury) and pesticides are major soil contaminants. Soil testing plays a vital role in enhancing agricultural productivity and pollution control. Besides PPM, PPB (Parts Per Billion) is also used to measure extremely low concentrations.

question:
The lava plateaus are rich in which kind of soil?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Laterite soil
Alluvial soil
Red soil
Black soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Black soil

Explanation:
Lava plateaus are predominantly rich in black soil (also known as regur soil), which is formed by the weathering of volcanic rocks, particularly basalt lava. This soil is highly fertile due to its high content of calcium, magnesium, potash, and lime, making it ideal for cotton cultivation. In India, it is primarily found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat). The soil has excellent moisture retention capacity, which supports crops even during dry spells.

Extra Facts:
Black soil is often called 'cotton soil' because it is best suited for cotton farming. Its dark color comes from iron oxide and titanium content. The soil becomes sticky when wet and develops deep cracks upon drying. In India, it covers about 16% of the cultivable land. Globally, it is also found in Brazil, Argentina, and Australia.

[SSC CPO 2023]

Lime

Explanation:
The black soil of the Deccan Plateau, also known as 'Regur Soil', is formed by the weathering of volcanic rocks. This soil is rich in minerals like iron, magnesium, lime, and potash, but it lacks phosphorous. This soil is ideal for cotton cultivation due to its high moisture retention capacity. Extra Facts:
Black soil is also called 'Cotton Soil' because it is most suitable for cotton cultivation. This soil also contains titanium and aluminium. When dry, it develops cracks, and when wet, it expands, making it easy to plough. The pH value of this soil ranges between 7.5 to 8.5, making it alkaline. The total area covered by black soil in India is approximately 5.18 lakh sq km.

question:
Which of the following soil particles are the finest in their size?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Sand
Silt
Pebble
Clay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Clay

Explanation:
Soil particle size varies by type. Clay has the finest particles, with a diameter of less than 0.002 mm. Due to its high water retention capacity, clay is highly fertile. Sand has the largest particles (0.05-2 mm), Silt is medium-sized (0.002-0.05 mm), and Pebble is very coarse (>2 mm). The microscopic structure of clay allows it to retain water and nutrients effectively.

Extra Facts:
Soil texture is crucial for agriculture, drainage, and construction. Clay exhibits shrink-swell properties due to high water content. In India, Black Soil (formed from volcanic rocks) is ideal for cotton cultivation, while Red Soil gets its color from iron oxides.

options_hi: लोम (Loam)
मार्ल (Marl)
लोएस (Loess)
पॉडसॉल (Podsol)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है लोएस (Loess)

Explanation:
लोएस (Loess) एक प्रकार की मिट्टी है जो गाद (silt) और धूल (dust) से बनी होती है। यह मुख्य रूप से हवा द्वारा जमा किए गए महीन कणों से निर्मित होती है। लोएस मिट्टी बहुत उपजाऊ होती है और इसमें जल धारण करने की क्षमता अधिक होती है। यह मिट्टी विशेष रूप से शुष्क और अर्ध-शुष्क क्षेत्रों में पाई जाती है, जहां हवा द्वारा महीन कणों का परिवहन होता है। चीन में 'ह्वांग हो' (पीली नदी) के आसपास का क्षेत्र लोएस मिट्टी का एक प्रमुख उदाहरण है।

Extra Facts:
लोएस मिट्टी का निर्माण पिछले हिमयुग (Ice Age) के दौरान हुए हिमनदों (glaciers) के कारण हुआ था। जब हिमनद पिघले, तो उन्होंने महीन गाद और धूल को जमा किया, जो बाद में हवा द्वारा उड़ाकर दूर-दूर तक फैल गए। यह मिट्टी आमतौर पर हल्के पीले या भूरे रंग की होती है और इसमें कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट की मात्रा अधिक होती है, जो इसे उपजाऊ बनाती है।

question:
Which of the following pairs regarding soil is correct?
I. Forest soil - These soils are loamy and silty in valley sides
II. Black soil - generally poor in phosphoric contents

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Both I and II
Only I
Only II
Neither I nor II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both I and II

Explanation:
Forest soil is indeed found on valley sides and is loamy and silty in texture. This soil is rich in organic matter due to the decomposition of vegetation. Black soil, also known as 'Regur soil', is generally poor in phosphoric content. It is highly suitable for cotton cultivation and is primarily found in the Deccan Plateau. Its high water retention capacity makes it drought-resistant.

Extra Facts:
Major soil types in India: Alluvial soil (most fertile), Black soil (suitable for cotton), Red soil (red due to iron oxide), Laterite soil (found in high rainfall areas), Desert soil (sandy). Soil conservation methods include contour ploughing, strip cropping, and afforestation.

question:
What do you call the weight a soil can withstand before severe damage occurs to the structure of the soil?

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Field capacity
Bearing capacity
Bulk density
Buffering capacity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bearing capacity

Explanation:
Bearing capacity refers to the maximum weight that soil can support without undergoing structural failure. It depends on the soil's physical and mechanical properties, such as particle size, compaction, and moisture content. This concept is crucial in foundation engineering, road construction, and agriculture as it determines the stability and safety of structures built on the soil.

Extra Facts:
Field capacity indicates the maximum water retained by soil, while bulk density is the ratio of soil mass to its volume. Buffering capacity refers to the soil's ability to resist changes in pH. These are distinct soil properties that play vital roles in agriculture and construction activities.

question:
Black soil is predominantly found in which one of the following states?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Maharashtra
Jharkhand
Karnataka
Odisha
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Maharashtra

Explanation:
Black soil, also known as 'Regur Soil' or 'Cotton Soil', is primarily found in the Deccan Plateau region. It is formed by the weathering of volcanic rocks and is rich in calcium, magnesium, potash, and lime. Maharashtra has the largest expanse of this soil, which is ideal for cotton cultivation. The soil has a high moisture retention capacity, supporting crops even during dry spells.

Extra Facts:
Black soil covers approximately 16% of India's total land area and is mainly distributed in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh. Its black color is due to the presence of titaniferous magnetite. This soil is deep and fertile, making it suitable for crops like sugarcane, soybeans, and cotton. It is well-suited to monsoon climatescrop rotation is essential to maintain its productivity.

question:
Punjab state is rich in which natural resource from the following ?

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Coal

Silicon
Fertile soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fertile soil

Explanation:
Punjab state is rich in fertile soil, also known as the 'Doab' region soil. This soil is found in the Indo-Gangetic plains and is an example of alluvial soil. It contains abundant nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potash, making it ideal for agriculture. Extra Facts:
Punjab's soil is of the alluvial type, formed by sediments deposited by rivers. The major rivers here are Satluj, Beas, and Ravi, which enrich the soil. Punjab also has a good groundwater level, useful for irrigation. The climate here is temperate, favorable for crops. Punjab has the highest percentage of cultivable land in India.

question:
Select the second step of decomposition.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: leaching
fragmentation
catabolism
humification
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is leaching

Explanation:
The second step of decomposition is leaching. This process involves the removal of soluble nutrients from organic matter by water. The first step is fragmentation, where large organic materials break down into smaller pieces. After leaching, catabolism occurs, followed by humification. This process plays a crucial role in maintaining soil fertility by recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.

Extra Facts:
Decomposition is vital for ecosystems as it facilitates nutrient recycling. During leaching, water transports soluble compounds like sugars and amino acids into the soil. Microorganisms and fungi are key players in this process. The rate of decomposition depends on factors like temperature, moisture, and oxygen availability. In tropical regions, decomposition occurs faster due to high humidity and temperature, whereas it slows down in colder climates.

question_hi:
अपघटन के दूसरे चरण का चयन करें।

[SSC GD 2022]

विखंडन
अपचय
आर्द्रीकरण
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है निक्षालन (leaching)

Explanation:
अपघटन (decomposition) की प्रक्रिया में दूसरा चरण निक्षालन (leaching) होता है। यह प्रक्रिया मृत जैव पदार्थों (organic matter) से घुलनशील पोषक तत्वों को पानी द्वारा बाहर निकालने की प्रक्रिया है। पहले चरण में विखंडन (fragmentation) होता है, जहां बड़े कार्बनिक पदार्थ छोटे-छोटे टुकड़ों में टूट जाते हैं। निक्षालन के बाद अपचय (catabolism) और अंत में आर्द्रीकरण (humification) होता है। यह प्रक्रिया मिट्टी की उर्वरता बनाए रखने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है।

Extra Facts:
अपघटन की प्रक्रिया पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (ecosystem) के लिए अत्यंत महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह पोषक तत्वों के पुनर्चक्रण (recycling) में सहायक होती है। निक्षालन के दौरान, जल घुलनशील यौगिकों जैसे शर्करा (sugars) और अमीनो अम्ल (amino acids) को मिट्टी में ले जाता है। इस प्रक्रिया में सूक्ष्मजीव (microorganisms) और कवक (fungi) महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाते हैं। अपघटन की दर तापमान, नमी और ऑक्सीजन की उपलब्धता पर निर्भर करती है।

The Parent rock is the most important factor in determining the colour, texture, chemical properties, mineral content, and permeability of the soil. Soil is formed by the weathering and disintegration of the parent rock. For example, black soil is formed from basalt rock, which is suitable for cotton cultivation. Similarly, red soil is formed from granite rock, which is red in colour due to the presence of iron oxide. The permeability of the soil also depends on the type of parent rock.

Extra Facts:
Other factors such as climate, time, relief, and biotic factors also play an important role in soil formation. Climate affects the rate of weathering of the soil, while time determines the maturity of the soil. Relief affects the depth and drainage of the soil. Biotic factors increase the fertility of the soil.

question:
Which soil is well known for its capacity to hold moisture?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Arid soil
Alluvial soil
Black soil
Laterite soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Black soil

Explanation:
Black soil, also known as 'Regur soil' or 'Cotton soil', is famous for its high moisture retention capacity. This soil is formed by the weathering of volcanic rocks and contains a high proportion of clay, which helps it retain water for long periods. It is primarily found in the Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat) and is suitable for crops like cotton, sugarcane, and soybean. Its ability to hold moisture helps sustain crops even during dry spells.

Extra Facts:
Black soil is rich in iron, magnesium, and alumina, making it highly fertile. It swells when wet and develops deep cracks when dry. This soil originates from basalt rocks and covers approximately 5.46 lakh sq km in India. It is particularly suitable for Kharif crops. The high clay content gives it a sticky texture when wet and makes it hard when dry.

question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding laterite soil?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options:
Red laterite soils in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala are more suitable for crops like cashew nut.

They are generally rich in humus.

This soil is very useful for growing tea and coffee.

The laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is They are generally rich in humus.

Explanation:
Laterite soil is found in tropical and subtropical regions with high temperatures and heavy rainfall. This soil is rich in iron and aluminum oxides but has low humus content because organic matter decomposes rapidly due to heavy rainfall. It is suitable for growing tea and coffee, especially in southern Indian states like Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka. The red color of laterite soil is due to the presence of iron oxides.

Extra Facts:
Laterite soil is formed due to weathering and leaching processes. It is found in the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and northeastern states of India. This soil is deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potash, making it less fertile for agriculture. However, with the use of fertilizers, crops like cashew, rubber, and coconut can be cultivated in this soil.

question:
______ develops on crystalline igneous rocks in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern part of the Deccan Plateau.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: Red soil
Black soil
Alluvial soil
Arid soil
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Red soil

Explanation:
Red soil develops on crystalline igneous rocks (such as granite and gneiss) in areas of low rainfall in the eastern and southern parts of the Deccan Plateau. The red color is due to the presence of iron oxide (Fe2O3). This soil is less fertile due to deficiencies in nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter. It is mainly found in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.

Extra Facts:
Characteristics of Red Soil:
- It is a mixture of sandy and clayey soil.
- It is rich in potash but deficient in phosphorus and nitrogen.
- Suitable for crops like cotton, groundnut, millets, and pulses.
- Covers about 10.6% of India's total land area.

question_hi:
दक्कन के पठार के पूर्वी और दक्षिणी भाग में कम वर्षा वाले क्षेत्रों में क्रिस्टलीय आग्नेय चट्टानों पर ______ विकसित होता है।

[SSC CGL 2021]
options_hi: लाल मिट्टी
काली मिट्टी
जलोढ़ मिट्टी
शुष्क मिट्टी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है लाल मिट्टी

Explanation:
दक्कन के पठार के पूर्वी और दक्षिणी भाग में कम वर्षा वाले क्षेत्रों में लाल मिट्टी विकसित होती है। यह मिट्टी क्रिस्टलीय आग्नेय चट्टानों (जैसे ग्रेनाइट और नीस) के अपक्षय से बनती है। लाल रंग लौह ऑक्साइड (Fe2O3) की उपस्थिति के कारण होता है। यह मिट्टी कम उर्वरक होती है क्योंकि इसमें नाइट्रोजन, फॉस्फोरस और जैविक पदार्थों की कमी होती है। यह मिट्टी मुख्य रूप से तमिलनाडु, कर्नाटक, आंध्र प्रदेश और ओडिशा में पाई जाती है।

Extra Facts:
लाल मिट्टी की विशेषताएँ:
- यह मिट्टी रेतीली और चिकनी मिट्टी का मिश्रण होती है।
- इसमें पोटाश की मात्रा अधिक होती है, लेकिन फॉस्फोरस और नाइट्रोजन की कमी होती है।
- यह मिट्टी कपास, मूंगफली, बाजरा और दालों की खेती के लिए उपयुक्त है।
- भारत में लाल मिट्टी का कुल क्षेत्रफल लगभग 10.6% है।
